support_text: The catfish hepatocytes were damaged at higher benzo[a]pyrene concentrations (>10^-6 M) as shown by transmission electron microscopy. The internal architecture of normal primary hepatocytes included large amounts of rough endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondria, glycogen, a few lipid droplets, and spherical nuclei with distinct nucleoli, providing the morphological baseline.

assay_context: biological_model_context=human sperm suspensions; Homo sapiens | assay_and_platform=chemiluminescence-based ROS measurement (reported in RLU)
endpoint: endpoint_class=reactive_species | endpoint_name=ROS (H2O2) production in sperm suspensions
qualifying_conditions: exposure_level=100 µmol/l | exposure_unit=µmol/l | treatment_and_comparator_context=single in-vitro exposure to APO; compared against sperm without APO; samples classified into low (LRP), normal (NRP), high (HRP) and very high (VHRP) ROS-production groups | extra_details=APO (NOX inhibitor) reduced ROS generation by almost 75-90% in HRP and VHRP and completely abolished ROS production in LRP and NRP samples (baseline ROS below 0.1 RLU); APO-induced prevention of ROS production caused cell death. | needs_more_context=False
support_text: APO (100 µmol/l), a NADPH oxidase (NOX) inhibitor, decreased ROS production to a considerable extent in all analysed human sperm samples. In HRP and VHRP samples, high ROS production was not completely abolished by APO, which affected almost 75-90% of ROS generation. In LRP and NRP samples, where baseline ROS production was below 0.1 RLU, APO completely abolished ROS production. APO-induced prevention of ROS production caused cell death.

assay_context: biological_model_context=normal human sperm; Homo sapiens | assay_and_platform=ROS evaluation in suspensions of capacitating sperm (NOX modulation conditions)
endpoint: endpoint_class=reactive_species | endpoint_name=ROS production (NADPH-stimulated NOX activation) in sperm
qualifying_conditions: exposure_level=10 µM | exposure_unit=µM | treatment_and_comparator_context=NADPH (increasing concentrations) added to activate NOX; 10 µM APO added to inhibit it; ROS measured during capacitation | extra_details=NADPH-induced NOX activation was partially or totally inhibited by 10 µM APO; ROS evaluation confirmed both the activation and gradual inactivation of the enzyme. | needs_more_context=False
support_text: Incubation of normal human sperm in conditions of NOX activity modulation showed that adding increasing concentrations of NADPH induced NOX activation, which was partially or totally inhibited by the addition of 10 µM APO. ROS evaluation confirmed both the activation and the gradual inactivation of the enzyme, and ARC percentages varied accordingly.
